name: Sika CarboDur M
paste:
SIKA® CARBODUR® M: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® CarboDur® M, April 2023, Version 05.04 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/6/sika_carbodur_m.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® CarboDur® M where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 05.04).
1.2 Product description.
    - Sika® CarboDur® M plates are pultruded carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminates, designed for strengthening concrete, timber, masonry, steel and fibre reinforced polymer structures.
    - Sika® CarboDur® M plates are bonded onto the structure as externally bonded reinforcement using Sikadur®-30 epoxy resin based adhesive for normal, or Sikadur®-30 LP* epoxy resin based adhesive for elevated temperatures during application and / or service, long lead times and quantities apply.
    - Please refer to the relevant Product Data Sheet for more detailed information about each of these adhesives.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Sika® CarboDur® M may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Sika® CarboDur® systems are used to improve, increase or repair the performance and resistance of structures for:
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Increased Load Carrying Capacity.
    - Increasing the load capacity of floor slabs, beams and bridge sections
    - For the installation of heavier machinery
    - To stabilise vibrating structures
    - For changes in building use
1.5 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Damage to structural elements due to.
    - Deterioration of the original construction materials
    - Steel reinforcement corrosion
    - Accidents (Vehicle impact, earthquakes, fire)
1.6 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Improvement of serviceability and durability.
    - Reduced deflection and crack width
    - Stress reduction in the steel reinforcement
    - Improved fatigue resistance
1.7 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Change of the structural system.
    - Removal of walls and / or columns
    - Removal of floor and wall sections to create access / openings
1.8 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Resistance to possible events.
    - Increased resistance to earthquakes, impact or explosion etc.
    - Insufficient / inadequate reinforcement
    - Insufficient / inadequate structural depth
    To repair design or construction defects such as:
1.9 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.4.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® CarboDur® M
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Pultruded Carbon Fibre Plates for Structural Strengthening as Part of the Sika® CarboDur® System- Type CLM(1) compliant to AS5100.8
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - Australia: AS5100.8- 2017 Bridge Design Part 8: Rehabilitation and strengthening of existing bridges.
    - Australia: Vic Roads Spec Section 688- Fibre Reinforced Polymer Composite Strengthening of Concrete Structures.
    - Slovakia: TSUS, Building Testing and research institutes,
    - Slovakia: Technical Approval TO-09/0080, 2009: Systémy dodatočného zosilňovania konštrukcií Sika® CarboDur® a SikaWrap®.
    - Poland: Technical Approval ITB AT-15-5604/2011: Zestaw wyrobów Sika® CarboDur® do wzmacniania i napraw konstrukcji betonowych
    - Poland: Technical Approval IBDiM Nr AT/2008-03- 0336/1 „Płaskowniki. pręty, kształtki i maty kompozytowe do wzmacniania betonu o nazwie handlowej: Zestaw materiałów Sika® CarboDur® do wzmacniania konstrukcji obiektów mostowych
    - France: CSTB - Avis Technique 3/16-875, Sika CarboDur, SikaWrap
    - Fib, Technical Report, bulletin 14: Externally bonded FRP reinforcement for RC structures, July 2001.
    - USA: ACI 440.2R-08, Guide for the Design and construction of Externally Bonded FRP Systems for strengthening concrete structures, July 2008.
    - UK: Concrete Society Technical Report No. 55, Design guidance for strengthening concrete structures using fibre composite material, 2000.
    - Switzerland: SIA 166, Klebebewehrungen, 2003 /2004.
    - Italy: CNR-DT 200 R1/2013 - Guide for the Design and Construction of Externally Bonded FRP Systems for Strengthening Existing Structures
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS5100.8- 2017: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 2561: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Laminate elongation at break in tension Mean value (p.2); Technical Information > Laminate modulus of elasticity in tension (p.2); Technical Information > Laminate tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN 61006: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Glass transition temperature (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Combination of very high strength and high stiffness
    - Non-corroding
    - Excellent durability and fatigue resistance
    - Unlimited lengths, no joints required
    - Low system thickness, simple execution of plate intersections or crossings
    - Easy transportation (rolls)
    - Lightweight, very easy to install, especially overhead (without temporary support)
    - Minimum preparation of plate, applicable in several layers
    - Smooth edges without exposed fibres as result of production by pultrusion
    - Extensive testing and approvals available from many countries worldwide
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance and colour: Carbon fibre reinforced polymer with an epoxy matrix, black.
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Fibre volume content: > 68%
    - Laminate elongation at break in tension Mean value: 1.7 % (EN 2561)
    - Glass transition temperature: >100 °C (EN 61006)
2.7 Dimensions.
    | Type Sika® CarboDur® | Width | Thickness          Cross section |
    | M | area |
    | 914 | 90 mm | 1.4 mm | 126 mm² |
    | 1214 | 120 mm | 1.4 mm | 168 mm² |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    * limited stocks available locally. Other sizes available on request. Minimum quantities may apply.
2.8 Laminate tensile strength.
    | Mean value | 3 500 N/mm² |
    | 5 % Fractile-value | 3 200 N/mm² |
    Test method printed: (EN 2561)
    Note printed: Values in the longitudinal direction of the fibres
2.9 Laminate modulus of elasticity in tension.
    | Mean value | 210 000 N/mm² |
    | 5 % Fractile-value | 205 000 N/mm² |
    Test method printed: (EN 2561)
    Note printed: Values in the longitudinal direction of the fibres
2.10 System structure. The system build-up and configuration as described must be fully complied with and may not be changed. Resin Adhesive - Sikadur®-30 or Sikadur®-30 LP*. Sikadur 30LP is a non stock item, lead times and minimum quantities apply. Structural strengthening Carbon plates – Sika® CarboDur® M. For detailed information on Sikadur®-30 and Sikadur®-30 LP*, together with the application details, please refer to the Sikadur®-30 or Sikadur®-30 LP* Product Data Sheet and the “Method Statement Sika® CarboDur® Externally Bonded Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 05.
2.11 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: Supplied in rolls of 100 m in non-returnable cardboard boxes. Material can be cut to order, lead times may apply.
    - Shelf life: Unlimited, provided the storage conditions are met.
2.12 Storage conditions. Store in original, unopened, sealed and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures of max. +50 °C. Protect from direct sunlight. Transportation: only in the original packaging, or otherwise adequately protected against any mechanical damage

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 05.04) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. Sika® CarboDur® plates externally bonded to the concrete surface; Recommended minimum concrete pull-off strength after surface preparation:
    - Mean: 2.0 N/mm²
    - Minimum: 1.5 N/mm²
    - CarboDur® applied in slots as near surface mounted (NSM) reinforcement
    - SikaWrap® fabrics: Please refer to the Product Data Sheet for the SikaWrap® fabrics
    The effective concrete pull-off strength after surface preparation has to be verified.
    If concrete pull-off strength is below the stated minimum requirements, alternative Sika solutions are available:
    Concrete must generally be older than 28 days (dependent on curing conditions and the type of concrete etc.)
    Sika® CarboDur® externally bonded to other substrates
    For application of CarboDur® plates to all other substrates (brick, stone, steel, wood, fibre reinforced polymer etc.) please refer to the “Method Statement for Sika® CarboDur® Externally Bonded Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 05. Contact Sika technical service for detailed advice.
3.3 Substrate preparation. Concrete must be cleaned and prepared to achieve a laitance and contaminant free, open textured surface. Please also refer to the “Method Statement Sika® CarboDur® Externally Bonded Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 05.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 05.04) and the requirements below.
4.2 Consumption.
    | Width of Sika® CarboDur® M plate | Typical consumption of |
    | Sikadur®-30* |
    | 50 mm | 0.20 − 0.28 kg/m |
    | 60 mm | 0.24 − 0.32 kg/m |
    | 90 mm | 0.40 − 0.56 kg/m |
    | 100 mm | 0.44 − 0.64 kg/m |
    | 120 mm | 0.45 − 0.80 kg/m |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Note printed: *Note: Consumption is for standard application only. Rough or uneven substrate surfaces, plate crossings, loss and wastage can lead to a higher adhesive consumption of up to 20 %.
4.3 Application method / tools. Please refer to the relevant Product Data Sheet:
    - Sikadur®-30
    CarboDur® plates can be cut with a Guillotine, diamond saw or a hacksaw. Correct PPE should be used to protect from breathing CFRP dust.
    Please refer to the “Method Statement Sika® CarboDur® Externally Bonded Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 05.
4.4 Limitations and important considerations. Please refer to the relevant Product Data Sheet of Sikadur® epoxy adhesive:
    - Sikadur®-30
    - Sikadur®-30 LP* non stock item, lead times and minimum quantities apply
    A suitably qualified Structural Engineer must be responsible for the design of the strengthening works. Additionally as this application is structural, great care must also be taken in selecting suitably experienced and trained specialist contractors.
    Sika® CarboDur® strengthening systems with Sika® CarboDur® plates must be protected from permanent exposure to direct sunlight, moisture and/or water. Please refer to the relevant Method Statement and Product Data Sheets for the selection of suitable over coating materials, in situations where systems will be fully or partially exposed.
    Maximum permissible continuous service temperature is approx. +50 °C.
    Note: When using the Sika CarboHeater* for curing
    Sikadur®-30 LP* to be used at elevated temperatures, the maximum continuous service temperature can be increased to max. +80 °C. Please also refer to the relevant Method Statements for further limitations and guidelines: - “Method Statement Sika CarboDur® Externally Bonded Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 05 Contact Sika technical service for detailed advice.
4.5 Further information. For structural design assistance of your next CFRP project, Sika can offer free of charge design software to assist in speeding up the design process. Software can be downloaded from Sika Australia's web site @ au.sika.com. For additional information call your local Sika branch in your state.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.4):
    - Sika® CarboDur® strengthening systems with Sika® CarboDur® plates must be protected from permanent exposure to direct sunlight, moisture and/or water. Please refer to the relevant Method Statement and Product Data Sheets for the selection of suitable over coating materials, in situations where systems will be fully or partially exposed.
    - Maximum permissible continuous service temperature is approx. +50 °C.
    - Sikadur®-30 LP* to be used at elevated temperatures, the maximum continuous service temperature can be increased to max. +80 °C. Please also refer to the relevant Method Statements for further limitations and guidelines: - “Method Statement Sika CarboDur® Externally Bonded Reinforcement” Ref: 850 41 05 Contact Sika technical service for detailed advice.
5.3 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Recommended minimum concrete pull-off strength after surface preparation:
    - The effective concrete pull-off strength after surface preparation has to be verified.
    - If concrete pull-off strength is below the stated minimum requirements, alternative Sika solutions are available:
5.4 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Laminate tensile strength: Mean value | 3 500 N/mm²; 5 % Fractile-value | 3 200 N/mm² (EN 2561)
    - Laminate modulus of elasticity in tension: Mean value | 210 000 N/mm²; 5 % Fractile-value | 205 000 N/mm² (EN 2561)
    - Laminate elongation at break in tension Mean value: 1.7 % (EN 2561)
    - Glass transition temperature: >100 °C (EN 61006)
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® CarboDur® M, April 2023, Version 05.04, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/6/sika_carbodur_m.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling,storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
